findings.text: Socket option setup reads a length from user space, rejects negative lengths, then prepares matching source and destination iterators over the same user buffer and records the length for later use, reporting user memory faults distinctly from invalid lengths.

Wake queue record holds a wait queue head that is required to lead the layout, an asynchronous notification list, flag bits for async space and data conditions, and a deferred freeing record, with SMP cacheline alignment to avoid sharing.

Socket record holds a state value, a small integer type, flag bits, references to an open file and a protocol socket object, a protocol operations pointer that may change for address form or multipath reasons, and an embedded wake queue object.
Read descriptor tracks how many bytes were written versus requested, a location that holds either a user buffer pointer or a kernel data pointer, and an error field for short or failed copies.

Protocol operations table groups lifecycle and I/O handlers for release, binding, connecting, pairing, accepting, naming, polling, control, timestamping, listening, shutdown, options, descriptor info, message send and receive, mapping, splicing, peek control and low-water tuning, plus a locked tail group for direct socket reads and buffer sizing.
Protocol family record pairs a numeric family identifier with a creation handler that builds a socket inside a network namespace from protocol and kernel-mode inputs, plus an owner module reference.

Socket types are numbered with STREAM as 1, DGRAM as 2, RAW as 3, RDM as 4, SEQPACKET as 5, DCCP as 6 and PACKET as 10, with an upper bound one past PACKET and a low nibble mask for extracting the type from combined creation flags.

Close-on-exec, nonblock and coredump creation flags alias the corresponding open file flags, shutdown directions order read then write then both, socket flag positions order async space then async data then space then zero-copy then custom options, and wake reasons order I/O then wait then space then urgent.

Device features form a 64-bit mask where each capability occupies one bit position defined by an ordered enumeration ending in a count sentinel, with a contiguous GSO subrange delimited by shift and last markers and single-bit construction by shifting one by the bit index.

Feature group masks fix which bits never change, which are visible to ethtool, which span checksums, segmentation, software segmentation, one-for-all and all-for-all propagation, upper-device disables, soft defaults, VLAN and encapsulation sets, and master upper-device inheritance for VLAN, encapsulation, MPLS, transform and partial segmentation cases.

Receive path uses success 0 and drop 1 with nesting depth 8, transmit path uses success 0 drop 1 and congestion 2 under a low nibble mask while driver returns use 0 for taken and 16 for busy under a high nibble mask, XDP features are 32 bits, link headers have build-dependent maxima of 128, 96 or 32 bytes and the network header maximum either equals that value or adds 48 bytes.

Receive handlers update the returned name length only when a name buffer was supplied, treat that length as zero by default to avoid leaking uninitialized memory, and may assume a supplied buffer offers at least storage-sized capacity.

The tail group for direct socket reading at descriptor or whole-packet granularity, locked sending, and receive buffer tuning is invoked internally with the socket lock already held, unlike the upper file-oriented operations.

Per-protocol entry points cover socket lifecycle, naming and connection setup, polling and control, option get and set including an iterator variant, message and splice transport, memory mapping, peek offset handling and length peeking, and show routines for descriptor introspection.

Family creation, socket address casting with compile-time size checking, and two read actor styles provide extension points: one delivering data incrementally through a descriptor, the other delivering one complete packet buffer at a time.

Rate-limited log helpers emit only when the network rate limiter allows, with debug builds selecting dynamic, plain or compiled-out behavior, random helpers delegate to one-time generators in blocking and sleepable forms, and module alias helpers encode protocol, family and type names for autoloading.

Feature iteration scans set bits from high to low by masking below the start position and locating the highest remaining bit, and base-feature normalization clears the one-for-all set before forcing the all-for-all set.

Transmit helpers normalize congestion to success for evaluation and to no-buffer errors otherwise, completion is signaled by values below the transmit mask including negative errors, socket file release drops the file reference, and page checks accept only non-slab pages with at least one reference across the byte range from an offset.

Option setup must handle faulting user length pointers and negative lengths, zero-copy page acceptance depends on slab state and reference count over every page spanned, and socket file teardown relies on file reference counting rather than direct socket freeing.
